A network path that starts with two backslashes (\server\share\data\tex.paa, also with forward slashes //server/...) is treated as absolute in PathMapper.map_path: it goes through the $PBOPREFIX$ and HEMTT rules, and when neither matches it gets the same warning as an unmatched drive-letter path instead of being silently changed. A path with one leading backslash (\a3\data\...) is still written as typed without that backslash, as today.

spec:
Research and design for the character rigging pipeline (owner, 2026-11-04). Goal: rigging a character for Arma 3 in Houdini as easy as possible: read the Arma skeleton, take a rigged sample mesh (Bohemia's A3_character_example.p3d by default), transfer the weights to the user's mesh, with hand fixing minimal or unnecessary in most cases. Output: one design document, docs/design/character-rigging.md (research findings + spec + phases with acceptance tests), no product code. Hython spikes are fine (headless only; never the owner's running Houdini); keep spike scripts under tests/ or scripts/spikes/ and cite their output. No Arma 3 Samples or game bytes committed.
Owner decisions so far (record them in the doc):
- The skeleton comes from a model.cfg the user points at (not hard-coded), with a skeleton picker (several CfgSkeletons classes, skeletonInherit). model.cfg's pivotsModel names a binarized game file, so the node also takes the path of an editable pivots .p3d (default: Arma 3 Samples TemplateRTM/ManSkeleton_Pivots.p3d, 65 body pivots).
- Face bones (36 Face_* + eyes) are out of scope for now.
- Layered weighting with three group fields: first pass (base clothing, full transfer from the sample body), rigid accessories (each connected piece gets its weights from the first-pass points it sits on: one dominant bone, or one fixed blend per piece), non-rigid accessories (bandoliers, cables: per-point transfer from the first pass, smoothed along the piece).
- A visualiser that highlights problems.
- Fit -> rig -> unpose: adjust the imported Arma skeleton (and/or the sample body) to match the user's mesh (appendages at slightly different angles, body larger or smaller), transfer weights there, then return the mesh to the Arma rest pose for export, so it sits on Arma's fixed pivots. Returning to the standard skeleton should fix scaling (bone length) differences automatically; find out how well that works and where it distorts (joints, rigid accessories).
1. Auto-rigging and alignment survey (owner priority): what others have done that can align Arma's fixed skeleton (fixed topology and names) to a new mesh, or fit the rigged sample body to it. Cover at least: (a) Houdini 22.0.466 native tools: KineFX/APEX (Autorig Builder, capture nodes, Rig Pose, Rig Match Pose, Map Points, Skeleton Blend, Full Body IK, any joint-placement or landmark tool, ML tools in 22.0); verify names and behaviour with the docs tool and hython, and say what works in Indie. (b) Template / registration methods: fitting the rigged sample body to the target (per-bone rigid fit down the hierarchy, non-rigid ICP / deformation transfer), Pinocchio-style skeleton embedding (Baran & Popovic 2007, embeds a given skeleton). (c) Learned auto-riggers (UniRig SIGGRAPH 2025, RigNet, Make-It-Animatable, others): whether their joint predictions could serve as landmarks for our fixed skeleton, their licences, and their runtime needs (GPU, PyTorch), and whether they can be an optional external step rather than part of the add-on. (d) Commercial tools (Mixamo, AccuRIG) only as reference for workflow. For each: fit with our fixed Arma skeleton, licence compatibility with GPL-3.0-or-later, dependencies inside hython 22 (numpy is there; check scipy and others), expected quality for uniforms on the standard body vs bodies with different proportions. Recommend one approach for phase 1 and one for later.
2. Weight transfer method: closest-point transfer with distance + normal thresholds and inpainting of unmatched points (Abdrashitov et al., "Robust Skin Weights Transfer via Weight Inpainting", SIGGRAPH Asia 2023) vs Houdini-native options (capture nodes, attribute transfer of unpacked capture weights). Feasibility in hython (sparse solve: scipy or a Houdini solver), speed on a 10k-point uniform, quality on a sample case (spike).
3. Arma rules, cited (BI community wiki, A3OB source in .reference/, the Samples): max bones per vertex (the sample never exceeds 4), weight steps (1/255), sums, which LODs need weights (the sample weights 4 visual LODs, View Pilot, 2 shadows, Hit points, Fire geometry rigid one bone, Memory), sections/model.cfg links, what happens in game when mesh joints are off the pivots. A3OB's rigging features inventory (armature from model.cfg/pivots, weights, RTM) with file refs.
4. Houdini data: KineFX skeleton and boneCapture format; mapping P3D bone selections <-> capture weights both ways; export clean-up (max 4, 1/255, normalise, prune) and how it reports what it changed.
5. Visualiser design: the problems it shows (filled-in vs copied points, weight jumps between neighbours, >4 influences before clean-up, rigid pieces straddling a joint, joints outside the mesh, pose stress test colouring stretch/compression in a few test poses), how it is shown (viewer state like the Mass visualiser, colours, attributes).
6. Node list with parameters and data flow; phases (suggested: 1 skeleton + weight conversion + export clean-up; 2 fit + transfer + layered groups + visualiser; 3 LOD propagation + mirroring; 4 RTM import for pose tests), each with acceptance tests; open questions for the owner, numbered.
title: Research + design: character rigging pipeline (Arma skeleton, auto-fit, weight transfer, visualiser)

spec:
Character rigging phase 1a: the Rig Skeleton node (design: docs/design/character-rigging.md sections 3, 4.1, 6.2, 6.3 phase 1; owner answers D37). Builds the Arma skeleton as a KineFX skeleton from a model.cfg and an editable pivots .p3d the user points at.
1. Design doc first: section 6.5 records the owner's answers (D37) under each question, and the sections that depend on them say the decided behaviour (A-pose input, landmarks as point groups, model.cfg spelling, adult humanoids, no skeleton changes for body shape).
2. Pure code in python/a3ob_core/rig/ (numpy allowed, D37 Q14): a model.cfg reader for CfgSkeletons (skeletonBones pairs, skeletonInherit, isDiscrete, pivotsModel; // and /* */ comments; class A: B; #include lines reported, not followed) and the pivot positions from a pivots P3D (its Memory LOD selections). Tests 1.2 and 1.3 of the design.
3. Rig Skeleton SOP (text HDA like the others): model.cfg file, skeleton picker (menu of the CfgSkeletons classes in that file), pivots .p3d file. Defaults come from the Samples path stored once in the project settings (D37 Q1: add an "Arma 3 Samples folder" field to the settings dialog and a3ob_settings.json; default the Steam path when it exists); empty fields show a clear error that says what to set. Output: KineFX skeleton, joints named with the model.cfg spelling, parents before children, each joint at its pivot, Face_* and Eye* left out (D36), Camera/weapon/launcher reported as missing pivots and left out, Hips reported and ignored (D37 Q4). Info line with the counts. Design test 1.1.
4. Run KineFX/APEX checks in plain hython WITHOUT HOUDINI_PACKAGE_SKIP=1 (it removes all kinefx::* types); tests still install the checkout's HDAs. Never the owner's running Houdini. No Samples bytes committed; Samples tests skip when absent (tests/samples_support.py).
5. User docs: reference page generated as usual; a short Rigging section in concepts.html (what the skeleton node needs and why the pivots file is separate). Tooltips plain.
6. quick gate passes on CPython 3.12 and hython 3.13; build_hdas.py --check and build_user_docs.py --check clean.
7. Wiki facts verified by the advisor in a browser, 2026-11-04 (record them in the design doc, replacing the "via search summary" marks): (a) BI "Arma 3: Modding Characters" says "use max 4 bones per vertex" and recommends transferring skinning from the example character (3ds Max Skin Wrap), the same idea as ours; helmets and glasses need an empty View Pilot LOD; a chin strap can be skinned to "Face_Jawbone". (b) BI "Model Config": skeletonBones are "<bone>", "<parent>" pairs with an empty parent for a root; skeletonInherit inherits all bones; isDiscrete = 1 means 0 or 100 % per vertex, 0 means partial weights; pivotsModel is marked "(A2 only)" on that page although the A3 Samples use it (note it; the owner's in-game tests, D37 Q9, decide whether off-pivot joints matter). Model cfg file naming: a <foldername>.cfg takes precedence over model.cfg, and <modelname>.cfg is read alongside; the node reads the one file the user picks, and its tooltip says so. (c) "P3D Named Selections" (unofficial, formulas "found by experimenting") gives conflicting decodes; the real files settle it: A3OB data_p3d.py decode_weight is (255 - b) / 254, and the sample's Resolution 1 has 201 distinct bytes with b = 2 never used, which rules out the page's 1 % step variant.
title: Rigging 1a: Rig Skeleton node (model.cfg + pivots .p3d -> KineFX skeleton)

Design test 1.4 (round trip of the sample Resolution 1 within 1/254) and 1.5 (Joint Deform at rest returns every point within 1e-5; one joint rotated equals a numpy linear blend skinning within 1e-5; settle and document the boneCapture_pCaptData layout).
2. Weight Cleanup SOP: at most 4 bones per point, weights on the k/254 grid with an exact sum of 1 (D37 Q2), tiny weights pruned (threshold parm, default from the design), points with no weight reported. Writes a3ob_rig_changed (the L1 change per point) and a message with the counts. Design test 1.6, including the sample's own sums (0.984 to 1.0) and its LOD with 29 points summing to 2.0.
3. Pure maths in python/a3ob_core/rig/ (numpy); passes under numpy 1.26 (CPython) and 2.3.2 (hython).
4. Plain hython without HOUDINI_PACKAGE_SKIP=1 for KineFX tests; never the owner's running Houdini; no Samples bytes committed.
5. Reference pages generated; concepts.html Rigging section extended (selections vs capture weights, what Cleanup changes). Plain tooltips.
6. quick gate passes on CPython 3.12 and hython 3.13; build_hdas.py --check and build_user_docs.py --check clean.
7. From the advisor's wiki check (2026-11-04, see #61 criterion 7): a byte 255 is a member with weight 0.0 (A3OB decodes it so; the sample has 14): Weights Convert and Cleanup treat it as no weight, and Cleanup reports such members. When the chosen skeleton has isDiscrete = 1, Cleanup gives every point exactly one bone (the heaviest), as the Model Config page defines discrete skinning, and says so in its message.

4. Mirror toggle, on by default: the right side follows the left, mirrored about the X = 0 plane (Left is +X), so dragging a left marker moves its right partner; off makes both sides free.
5. Shortcut: a landmark can be set from the points selected in the viewport (their average), for chin and groin mainly; the point selection is not stored, only the position.

The lm_* point-group path is removed (one way to set landmarks; nothing has been released). Snap still applies to chin and groin. 1. Bug (owner, 2026-11-05, Character_74_landmarks.hiplc): the fitted skeleton kinks between Pelvis and Spine. In the Arma rest Pelvis and Spine are in the same place (0,0,0), but after Rig Fit Pelvis is at y=1.034 and Spine at y=0.962 (7 cm apart), so the chain zigzags Pelvis -> Spine (down) -> Spine1 (up). Cause (advisor read): python/a3ob_core/rig/fit.py joint_targets averages the Pelvis target with a groin-based estimate, but Spine keeps the plain torso-frame target. Fix so joints that share a place in the Arma rest share it after the fit (Pelvis and Spine at least; check every zero-length rest bone in the hierarchy), keeping the groin's influence if it is still wanted.
2. Tests: on the owner scene and on the design test 2.3 setup, every zero-length rest bone is zero-length after the fit (under 1 mm); the Pelvis -> Spine -> Spine1 chain has no reversal. Fit-quality message and design tests 2.1-2.4 still pass; report the before/after quality numbers on the owner scene.
3. Owner scene: no rebuild needed (the fit cooks from the landmarks); confirm in a fresh hython on Character_74_landmarks.hiplc that Pelvis and Spine coincide. D38: never overwrite exportTests/Character.hiplc. quick gate and samples gate pass.
title: Rig Fit bug: Pelvis and Spine split apart (kink) after the fit
